new_statements.translation: 3.10 Suprasegmental phonemes. Phonemes that could be classed as suprasegmental turn out not to be found in the Dusun Deyah language. Stress, pitch and the like are not meaning-distinguishing.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the held file via its extracted text layer (.txt, lines 1162-1165) and the 150-dpi page render printed p.22 = PDF p.37). The page image reads exactly: '3.10 Fonem Suprasegmental / Fonem yang dapat digolongkan sebagai suprasegmental ternyata tidak dijumpai dalam bahasa Dusun Deyah. Tekanan, nada, dan sejenisnya tidak bersifat membedakan arti.' -- the reported quote is verbatim (the scanned layer has trivial garbles 'nada;' 'sejeriisnya' 'artj;' but the scan itself matches word for word). I read the rest of Bab III Fonologi (TOC 3.1 Konsonan... 3.10, printed pp.13-22; txt lines ~740-1166): consonant/vowel/diphthong inventories with minimal pairs, phoneme distribution, syllable canon (K…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only prosodic statement in the sole grammar: stress (and pitch, length) is non-contrastive/non-phonemic in Dusun Deyah. The position of (phonetic) word stress is NOT stated anywhere in the book, so no fixed-position reading can be assigned from this source.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about phonemic status only (word-level lexical contrast); no phonetic placement rule, no phrase-level remarks beyond sentence-intonation notes in the syntax chapter.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1983 grammar describes Dusun Deyah as spoken in Kecamatan Haruai (desa Pangelak, Kinarum, Kaong, Bilas) and Kecamatan Muara Uya, Kabupaten Tabalong, Kalimantan Selatan = Glottolog dusu1271 (ISO dun) exactly; Hudson 1967 spells it 'Dusun Dejah' (informant from Mengkopong). No dialect split relevant to the statement.

sources.note: Bab III Fonologi pp.13-22; sec. 3.10 'Fonem Suprasegmental' (p.22): no suprasegmental phonemes are found; stress, pitch and the like do not distinguish meaning. No statement of where stress falls; no stress marks in transcriptions; 'tekanan' otherwise appears only in the fieldwork questionnaire appendix (pp.128-131).
